title: Alternate day versus consecutive day oral iron supplementation in iron ...
abstract:
The study investigated iron absorption from oral iron supplements in iron-depleted women, comparing consecutive versus alternate-day dosing. It found that iron absorption was approximately 36% higher with alternate-day dosing, based on changes in serum ferritin. However, despite this increased absorption, the consecutive-day group had higher serum ferritin levels at 3 months, suggesting that the increased absorption with alternate-day dosing did not fully compensate for the lower total iron dose provided over that period. This could be due to higher obligatory body iron losses over a longer duration or the gradual reduction in iron absorption as iron stores replenished.

The study also examined gastrointestinal (GI) side effects. Using a mobile application for daily self-reporting, it confirmed that alternate-day dosing was associated with fewer GI side effects compared to consecutive-day dosing. Specifically, the prevalence of nausea, stomach pain, and overall side effects was significantly lower with alternate-day dosing.

Regarding dosing regimens, the study did not directly compare single morning doses versus twice-daily split dosing. However, it did note that previous studies have suggested that the dosing regimen, rather than the dose itself, influences GI side effects.
